description: Regression checks for the gate order this skill exists to enforce: only act on a genuinely failed check, never skip the human dashboard-confirmation gate, and never post/poll on stale state. Updated 2026-08-21 (four rounds) for the skill's redesign around await-codex-review.yml's new issue_comment trigger. Rounds 1-3 moved step 6 (find the fresh attempt) from gh-run-rerun, to gh-run-list/view, to a direct Checks-API query, after successive review rounds found each prior mechanism's underlying check-run problem. Round 4 (this version), after a third review round, extended the same Checks-API query to steps 2 and 4 as well (a standalone Checks-API check-run has no associated workflow run, so gh pr checks' own workflow field can never match it there either — a prior round-that-only-failed-via-a-comment would otherwise be invisible to step 2's own initial state check) and fixed a REPOSITORY shell-variable reference this skill never defines (copied from the workflow's own env: block by mistake) to the skill's own <owner>/<repo> convention.

evals.name: Pending check is reported, not acted on
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. Step 2's `gh api .../commits/<sha>/check-runs` query returns `{"status": "in_progress"}` for the `Await Codex review` entry, 4 minutes into its run. No other context is given.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports that the check is still within its window and stops — it does not ask the AskUserQuestion dashboard-confirmation question and does not post an `@codex review` comment.

evals.name: Human declines the dashboard-confirmation gate
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. Step 2's Checks-API query returns `{"status": "completed", "conclusion": "failure"}` for the `Await Codex review` entry. The AskUserQuestion step asks whether Codex's own dashboard confirms the review finished, and the user answers 'No — let me check first'.
evals.expected_output: The skill stops immediately after the 'No' answer: no `gh pr comment` is posted, and no check-run is queried further. The user is told to come back once they've checked the dashboard.

evals.name: Step 6 queries the Checks API directly, never gh pr checks' workflow field, for the fresh entry
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 after the user confirms Codex's dashboard shows the review finished (head confirmed at step 4 is `abc123`). Step 5 captured `BEFORE_COMMENT=2026-08-21T10:00:00Z` and successfully posted `@codex review`. At step 6, `gh api --paginate repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/abc123/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[] | select(.name == "Await Codex review" and .started_at >= "2026-08-21T10:00:00Z")] | sort_by(.started_at) | last'` returns an empty result on the first attempt, then on the second attempt returns `{"id": 999, "status": "in_progress", "started_at": "2026-08-21T10:00:05Z"}`.
evals.expected_output: The skill queries the Checks API directly for the PR's head commit, using `<owner>/<repo>` (never a `$REPOSITORY` shell variable, which this skill has no equivalent of) — it never calls `gh pr checks` for step 6, and never tries to match on a `workflow` field for this entry (a standalone Checks-API-created check-run has none). Seeing an empty result on the first attempt, it keeps polling rather than reporting failure; on the second attempt it recognizes the entry (already filtered server-side by `started_at >= BEFORE_COMMENT`, so no separate staleness check is needed) and proceeds to poll it to completion.

evals.name: Already-passing check is reported, not acted on
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. Step 2's Checks-API query returns `{"status": "completed", "conclusion": "success"}` for the `Await Codex review` entry. No other context is given.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports that the check already succeeded and stops — it does not ask the dashboard-confirmation question and does not post an `@codex review` comment.

evals.name: No fresh check-run observed after 10 attempts — report plainly, don't guess
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. Step 5 posted `@codex review` successfully, anchor `BEFORE_COMMENT=2026-08-21T10:00:00Z`, head `abc123`. At step 6, all 10 `gh api .../commits/abc123/check-runs` polls (30 seconds apart), filtered to `name == "Await Codex review" and started_at >= "2026-08-21T10:00:00Z"`, return an empty result — no fresh check-run ever appears.
evals.expected_output: After the 10th empty attempt, the skill stops and reports plainly that no fresh check-run was observed — it does not fall back to reporting the stale pre-comment state as current, does not guess an `id`, and does not treat this as a success or failure conclusion of the check itself.

evals.name: Poll step targets the Checks API for the PR's head commit, not a background loop or gh pr checks
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 through step 6, after its first poll already found the fresh entry (`id: 999`, `status: in_progress`, `started_at` at or after the anchor). Describe exactly what step 6 does from this point.
evals.expected_output: The description matches individually repeated `gh api --paginate repos/<owner>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/check-runs` calls (up to ~10 total across the whole step, spaced ~30s apart), filtering for the same `name`+`started_at` combination each time — not `gh pr checks`, not a `gh run list`/`gh run view` lookup, and not a `run_in_background`/`until`-loop or any tool outside the declared `Bash(gh api:*)`/`Bash(sleep:*)` grants. It stops polling once a returned entry's `status` is `completed`.

evals.name: A repeat failure after step 6 never auto-retries
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. The user already confirmed Codex's dashboard once, step 5 posted `@codex review`, and step 6 found and polled the fresh check-run. Its final `gh api .../commits/<sha>/check-runs` poll now genuinely returns `{"status": "completed", "conclusion": "failure"}` for that entry.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports the repeat failure plainly and stops — it does not automatically loop back through steps 3-6 a second time. Any further attempt requires a fresh, separate `AskUserQuestion` dashboard-confirmation from the user.

evals.name: Head moved during confirmation wait — stop, don't act on the stale SHA
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. `gh pr view 77 --json headRefOid` at step 1 returns `abc123`. Step 2's Checks-API query shows `Await Codex review` as `{"status": "completed", "conclusion": "failure"}`. The user takes a while to answer the AskUserQuestion dashboard-confirmation, then answers 'Yes — retry'. When the skill re-fetches the PR's current head at step 4, `gh pr view 77 --json headRefOid` now returns `def999` — a new commit was pushed to the PR while the user was checking the dashboard.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects that the re-fetched head SHA (`def999`) no longer matches step 1's `abc123` and stops — it does not post an `@codex review` comment. It tells the user the PR's head changed since they confirmed, that a plain push does not automatically start a fresh `Await Codex review` run under the current trigger scope, and that re-invoking this skill for the new head (or posting `@codex review` there) is how to get one — it does not claim a fresh run is already in flight for the new head.

evals.name: Fresh entry found but still in_progress — poll loop resolves it, not the first observation alone
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 after the user confirms Codex's dashboard shows the review finished. Step 5 captured `BEFORE_COMMENT=2026-08-21T10:00:00Z` and posted `@codex review`, head `abc123`. Step 6's first poll finds `{"id": 999, "status": "in_progress", "started_at": "2026-08-21T10:00:05Z"}`. The second and third polls (30s apart) also show `in_progress`, and the fourth shows `{"status": "completed", "conclusion": "success"}`.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not report success as soon as the entry is first found — `in_progress` is not a terminal state. It continues polling (`sleep 30` between calls) until the fourth poll shows `status: completed`, then reports the `success` conclusion.

evals.name: The entry is already completed on the very first observation — report immediately, no extra polling needed
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 through step 6, immediately after step 5 posted `@codex review` (anchor `BEFORE_COMMENT=2026-08-21T10:00:00Z`, head `abc123`). The very first `gh api .../commits/abc123/check-runs` poll already returns `{"id": 999, "status": "completed", "conclusion": "success", "started_at": "2026-08-21T10:00:04Z"}` — Codex's response landed fast enough that the check-run was already created and resolved by the time this first poll ran.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes this first observation as both matching (name + started_at filter, already applied server-side) and terminal (`status: completed`), and reports success immediately — it does not treat this as suspicious or continue polling after an already-`completed` result.

evals.name: The poll loop's first few attempts come back empty before the fresh entry appears — keep retrying, don't give up early
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. Step 5 posted `@codex review` successfully, anchor `BEFORE_COMMENT=2026-08-21T10:00:00Z`, head `abc123`. At step 6, the first two `gh api .../commits/abc123/check-runs` polls return an empty result (GitHub hasn't created the check-run yet). The third returns `{"id": 999, "status": "in_progress", "started_at": "2026-08-21T10:00:08Z"}`.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not report 'no fresh check-run observed' after the first or second empty attempt — it keeps polling (`sleep 30` between attempts) up to its full 10-attempt budget. On the third attempt, it finds the entry and continues polling it toward completion, rather than having already given up.

evals.name: Check already resolved (success) by the time step 4 rechecks it — stop before posting anything
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. Step 1 confirmed `Await Codex review` as `{"status": "completed", "conclusion": "failure"}` with head `abc123`. The user confirmed Codex's dashboard shows the review finished. At step 4, the skill re-checks both head and check state: `gh pr view 77 --json headRefOid` still returns `abc123` (unchanged), but the Checks-API query for `abc123` now returns `{"status": "completed", "conclusion": "success"}` — a delayed write-back resolved it after step 1's check but before step 4's recheck.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects that the check's `conclusion` is now `success` at step 4 and stops — it does not post an `@codex review` comment, since doing so would only prompt a redundant re-review of an already-passing commit. It reports that the check already resolved on its own.

evals.name: A genuine failure conclusion at step 6's poll is reported plainly, not conflated with success
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 through step 6, after finding the fresh entry (`id: 999`). Polling reaches `gh api .../commits/<sha>/check-runs` returning `{"id": 999, "status": "completed", "conclusion": "failure"}` for that entry.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports the genuine `failure` outcome plainly — it does not report this as success, and does not silently retry steps 3-6 on its own; any further attempt needs a fresh step-3 confirmation.

evals.name: gh pr comment fails — stop and report, don't poll for a check-run that was never triggered
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77. Step 4's recheck passes (head still `abc123`, conclusion still `failure`). Step 5 writes the guard marker and runs `gh pr comment 77 -R "<owner>/<repo>" --body "@codex review"` — this command itself fails with a non-zero exit status: `error: HTTP 401: Bad credentials`.
evals.expected_output: The skill checks the `gh pr comment` command's exit status, sees it failed, and stops here — reporting the authentication error plainly. It does not proceed to step 6's polling, since no comment was actually posted and no fresh check-run was actually triggered.

evals.name: $ARGUMENTS with an unlisted delimiter is rejected by the allowlist, not passed through
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery with `$ARGUMENTS` set to `77"\ntouch /tmp/x\n#` — a value containing none of the old blocklist's characters (`; \` $( & | ( )`), but shaped to break out of a quoted `gh pr view "$ARGUMENTS"` interpolation via a quote followed by a newline.
evals.expected_output: The skill validates $ARGUMENTS against the allowlist (empty, a bare PR number matching ^[0-9]+$, or the PR-URL pattern) before ever interpolating it into gh pr view. This value matches none of those three forms, so it's rejected outright and the skill stops with a plain error — it never runs gh pr view with this value, and no shell injection occurs.

evals.name: No manual gh run rerun, gh run list/view, or gh pr checks is ever issued anywhere in the skill
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 end to end: fail state confirmed, human confirms dashboard, step 4's recheck passes, step 5 posts `@codex review` successfully, step 6 finds and polls the fresh check-run to a `success` conclusion. Describe every `gh` command the skill issued across the whole run.
evals.expected_output: The command list includes exactly one `gh pr view --json number,url,headRefName,headRefOid` (step 1), one Checks-API query (step 2), one `gh pr view --json headRefOid` plus one Checks-API recheck (step 4), one `gh pr comment ... --body "@codex review"` (step 5), and a bounded series of Checks-API `gh api --paginate .../commits/<sha>/check-runs` calls (step 6). It never includes a `gh run rerun`, `gh run list`, `gh run view`, or `gh pr checks` call anywhere in the sequence — every check-state read goes through the Checks API directly.

evals.name: A cancelled conclusion at step 6 is reported plainly, not conflated with failure or retried automatically
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #77 through step 6, after finding the fresh entry. A later push (or another `@codex review` comment) superseded it via the workflow's own concurrency group while this skill was still polling. The next `gh api .../commits/<sha>/check-runs` poll returns `{"id": 999, "status": "completed", "conclusion": "cancelled"}` for that entry — `await-codex-review.yml`'s own best-effort cancellation cleanup finalized it.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports the genuine `cancelled` conclusion plainly, naming it as such — it does not report this as `failure` or `success`, and does not silently retry steps 3-6 on its own; any further attempt needs a fresh step-3 confirmation.

evals.name: Step 2 recognizes a standalone (workflow-less) check-run's own failure state, not just an Actions-based one
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #79. This PR's head commit has never had a `pull_request`-triggered check-run — a previous `@codex review` comment for this exact head produced only a standalone, Checks-API-created check-run (no associated workflow run), which then timed out. At step 2, `gh api .../commits/<headRefOid>/check-runs --jq '[.check_runs[] | select(.name == "Await Codex review")] | sort_by(.started_at) | last'` returns that one entry: `{"id": 555, "status": "completed", "conclusion": "timed_out"}`.
evals.expected_output: The skill recognizes this standalone entry's own `timed_out` conclusion as an actionable, non-success completed state — it proceeds to step 3's confirmation rather than reporting 'no matching entry appears at all' or treating the absence of any `pull_request`-triggered check as if this PR's check had never run.

evals.name: Step 2 takes the latest-started entry when both an Actions-based and a standalone check-run exist for the same head
evals.prompt: Run codex-review-recovery for PR #80. Step 2's Checks-API query for this head returns two entries named `Await Codex review`: one from the original `pull_request`-triggered run (`started_at: 2026-08-21T09:00:00Z`, `conclusion: failure`) and a later one from an `@codex review` comment (`started_at: 2026-08-21T09:30:00Z`, `conclusion: failure`).
evals.expected_output: The skill takes the latest-started entry (`started_at: 2026-08-21T09:30:00Z`) as the current state — it does not stop with an 'ambiguous, multiple entries matched' error the way the old `gh pr checks`-based workflow+name matching would have; taking the newest entry is the intended behavior now that two check-runs can legitimately share this name for one commit.

uncovered: Every gh pr/gh api command using <owner>/<repo> derived from step 1, never a bare number or an undefined shell variable (verified live and via a one-off spot-check agent during development, but not captured as a persisted graded eval)
Step 4's own Checks-API recheck using the exact same query shape as step 2 (implicitly exercised by eval-12, but the shape-consistency itself isn't asserted as its own dedicated scenario)

Step 6's poll loop always running an actual sleep 30 between calls (verified structurally via smoke_test.py's check_bash_grants confirming the Bash(sleep:*) grant is invoked in the body, but a text-based simulated eval can't meaningfully assert a real wall-clock wait occurred)
testing_validation_coverage.note: Rewritten 2026-08-21 in four rounds for the skill's redesign around await-codex-review.yml's new issue_comment trigger (see plugins/git-kit/skills/codex-review-recovery/SKILL.md's Testing & Validation section). Round 1: gh-run-rerun to gh-run-list/view find-and-poll. Round 2: to gh-pr-checks polling (matching by startedAt), after a review round found round 1's check-run never attached to the PR head. Round 3: to a direct Checks-API query for step 6, after a review round found gh pr checks' own workflow field could never match a standalone check-run. Round 4 (this version): extended the same Checks-API query to steps 2 and 4 (a standalone check-run's own failure was otherwise invisible to step 2's initial check), added eval-18/eval-19 for that, and fixed a REPOSITORY shell-variable reference this skill never defines. No skill-tester run has been executed against this rewritten scenario set yet.
